oneLiner: The broadest wafer-fab equipment franchise, now valued like a cyclical one or two quarters from its peak even as management guides a second record year. The market is betting that AI-driven fab spending rolls over in 2027; the stock works if calendar 2027 is merely mid-cycle.

verdict.summary: The view moves up a notch from August, when a record quarter was already paid for: since then estimates have risen (a Q1 FY2027 guide of $11.1B and a first calendar-2027 call for 30%+ industry growth) while the sector de-rated sharply on AI-capex and rate fears. Our base case - FY2027 revenue near $46.5B at a low-20s multiple - is worth only modestly more than today, so this is a skew call, not a bargain call: the bull case adds roughly half, the bear case (a 2027 capex digestion valued at a mid-teens peak multiple) loses about a third. Two things would change the view: any customer pushout or a flat-to-down sequential guide before mid-2027, and gross margin slipping below 50% while capex and headcount keep climbing.
wtb: FY2027 (53 weeks, ending Oct 2027) revenue reaches at least ~$45B, +31% - output has to rise every quarter from the $11.1B Q1 guide, as management says it will.
Non-GAAP gross margin holds at or above 50.5% through the capacity ramp (Q1 FY2027 guide ~50.8%).
No pushouts from the big four customers through mid-2027, and hyperscaler 2027 capex guides rise again in the late-January 2027 reports.
At end-2027 the market still pays about 20x or more on FY2027 EPS, which only requires FY2028 to look flat to up, not down.

bear.why: Hyperscaler capex digests in mid-2027 and memory makers slow DRAM adds; quarterly revenue stalls near $10B after Q1 so FY2027 grows only ~19%. Ramp costs (hiring, new capacity) land on a flat revenue line and net margin slips to ~30%. The market calls FY2027 the peak and pays a mid-teens peak-cycle multiple; the sector has traded in single digits at past peaks.

base.why: Output rises each quarter from the $11.1B Q1 guide (roughly $11.1B, $11.3B, $11.8B, $12.3B), +35% for the year and consistent with 30%+ calendar-2027 industry growth. Net margin ~32%, in line with Q4 FY2026. FY2028 visibility is decent but not certain, so the multiple sits near the five-year average rather than at the mid-2026 peak.

bull.why: Clean-room and supply pinch points ease, DRAM/HBM, leading-edge logic and packaging all run above plan and Applied gains share; revenue +45% with net margin ~33.5% on operating leverage. Fab projects opening in 2029-2030 make FY2028 another growth year and the market pays a growth multiple, still well below the mid-2026 peak.

scenarioModel.note: EPS = revenue x net margin / ~790M diluted shares (798M in Q4 FY2026, less buybacks): bear $41.0B x 30.0% = $12.3B -> $15.6; base $46.5B x 32.0% = $14.9B -> $18.8; bull $50.0B x 33.5% = $16.8B -> $21.2. EPS is on a non-GAAP basis (excludes marks on strategic investments). FY2026 for reference: revenue $34.45B, non-GAAP EPS $12.89. Multiples are applied to FY2027 EPS at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Is calendar 2027 the peak of the equipment cycle, or the middle?
debates.bull: Management's first 2027 call (Nov 12, 2026): wafer-fab equipment up more than 30% to another record, Applied outgrowing it, output up every quarter, customers asking to pull deliveries in and no pushouts. It tracks 20+ fab ramps for 2027 and has added 10+ projects to its fab tracker for three straight quarters, many opening in 2029-2030; Lam still sees 2027 industry spending above $200B.
debates.bear: Revenue growing 50%+ YoY is what cycle peaks look like, and the customers' customers are stretched: the four largest AI buyers spent about $1.15 of capex per dollar of operating cash last quarter (Trefis). Equipment orders are the first thing cut, and the sector multiple fell to ~8x at the 2018 peak.
debates.view: We side with mid-cycle through 2027: the guide rests on rolling eight-quarter customer forecasts and supply, not demand, is the limiter. But the de-rating is the market front-running 2028, so this debate sets the multiple (15x vs 27x) more than the FY2027 number. Own it, sized for a 35-40% drawdown case.

signpost.metric: Q2 FY2027 revenue guide vs the $11.1B Q1 guide, and combined 2027 capex guidance from MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META
signpost.threshold: bullish if Q2 is guided above $11.1B despite one fewer week and capex is guided up 30%+; bearish on a sequential decline or any disclosed pushout
signpost.when: Hyperscaler Q4 calls late Jan 2027; AMAT Q1 FY2027 report mid-Feb 2027

debates.q: Can margins expand while Applied doubles its capacity?
debates.bull: Non-GAAP gross margin has risen YoY for 14 straight quarters and operating margin hit a record in Q4 FY2026 with opex at 15.2% of revenue; management cites mix, pricing and leverage and targets ~54% gross and ~40% operating margin by 2030 (Oct 13, 2026 investor day).
debates.bear: The investment burden is real: FY2026 capex was $2.67B, 7.8% of revenue versus about 3% in 2022, headcount rose 14% to 41.5K, and the plan is to double systems output by 2028 and more than double manufacturing and lab capacity by 2030 on top of the $5B EPIC center. Free cash flow was $6.2B, only ~61% of GAAP net income, and all of that fixed cost stays if revenue stalls.
debates.view: The spending is justified while every quarter is supply-limited, and the margin record so far says it is being absorbed. It is also the reason the bear case cuts margin as well as revenue. We accept lower cash conversion for one more year, not two.

signpost.metric: Non-GAAP gross margin and capex as % of revenue
signpost.threshold: gross margin below 50% or capex above 8% of revenue for two quarters = ramp is costing more than it earns
signpost.when: Q1 and Q2 FY2027 reports (mid-Feb and mid-May 2027)

debates.q: Does China fade gently or get cut off?
debates.bull: China was 25% of Q4 FY2026 revenue ($2.64B) and 27% of FY2026, down from the mid-30s a year earlier, and growth elsewhere has more than absorbed it. Management expects China to keep growing in dollars but fall below 25% of the business in 2027, with mature-node demand recovering mainly outside China. The $253M BIS export-control settlement was booked in FY2026 and closes that matter.
debates.bear: A quarter of revenue still sits one rule away from a step-down: the MATCH Act (introduced Apr 2026, would extend controls to servicing and more DUV-era tools) and the suspended BIS affiliates rule are both unresolved (status since mid-2026 unverified), and the post-midterm Congress is no friendlier to chip exports.
debates.view: A manageable drag, not a thesis-breaker: each 5 points of China share lost is roughly $2B of FY2027 revenue, inside the gap between our base and bear cases. It becomes a problem only if it lands at the same time as an AI digestion.

signpost.metric: China share of quarterly revenue; MATCH Act or affiliates-rule action
signpost.threshold: below 20% in a single quarter, or a servicing ban enacted, moves base toward bear
signpost.when: Each quarterly report; lame-duck session Nov-Dec 2026 and the new Congress in early 2027

thesis: Guided through a second record year. Management is steering to calendar-2027 industry growth above 30% with Applied outgrowing it, after Semiconductor Systems grows more than 40% in calendar 2026; customers are pulling deliveries in, not pushing out.

Mix is moving to the highest-intensity steps. DRAM rose to 33% of Semiconductor Systems revenue in Q4 FY2026, advanced packaging is growing ~90% and inspection/metrology 50%+ in calendar 2026; management says ~75% of industry growth through 2030 comes from DRAM, leading-edge logic and packaging, where Applied is strongest.
Operating leverage is showing. Semiconductor Systems non-GAAP operating margin reached 39.0% in Q4 FY2026 from 29.6% a year earlier, and EPS grew almost twice as fast as revenue.
Services compound underneath. AGS grew 26% YoY in Q4 at a 30.5% operating margin, is guided to its first $2B quarter and to mid-teens growth in 2027, with a 2030 target above $12B.

De-rated into rising estimates. The multiple compressed toward its five-year average in the Oct-Nov 2026 sector selloff while the company beat and raised; the reverse DCF needs only ~8% a year of earnings growth for a decade.
risks: Cyclical peak. Equipment downturns have cut the stock by more than half three times since 2007 and chipmakers cut tool purchases by almost two-thirds in 2008-09; if 2028 looks down, FY2027 EPS gets a peak multiple whatever it turns out to be.

Rising investment burden. Capex ran at 7.8% of FY2026 revenue (about 3% in 2022) with capacity doubling still ahead; the fixed cost is being added at what may be the top of the cycle and free cash flow trails earnings.

Earnings quality below the operating line. Net income ran at or above operating income through the first nine months of FY2026 because of roughly $0.95B of unrealized gains on strategic investments and a ~12-13% tax rate; Q4 reversed $653M of those marks, cutting GAAP EPS to $3.40 against $4.16 non-GAAP. Judge the business on operating income, and note that the planned increase in the Besi stake to ~20% adds more mark-to-market noise.
Export controls. China is a quarter of revenue and the MATCH Act and BIS affiliates rule remain open; a servicing ban would hit AGS, the steadiest profit stream.

Concentrated, debt-funded demand. A handful of buyers (TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix, Micron, Intel) place the orders and their spending now depends on hyperscaler capex that exceeds operating cash flow; a single pause is material.

latestProse: Q4 FY2026 (ended Oct 25, 2026; reported Nov 12). Revenue of $10.41B was a record, +53% YoY and +14% sequentially, ahead of the $10.25B guide midpoint and ~$10.30B consensus. Non-GAAP gross margin was 50.6% and GAAP operating margin 35.1%, a record, on $3.66B of operating income. Non-GAAP EPS of $4.16 beat the $4.02 guide; GAAP EPS was $3.40 because a $653M unrealized loss on strategic investments ran through other income. Semiconductor Systems did $8.00B (+64%) with DRAM at 33% of the mix, AGS $1.90B (+26%), and China fell to 25% of revenue. Cash generation set records ($3.30B operating, $2.62B free) and $2.4B went back to shareholders. Fiscal 2026 closed at $34.45B of revenue (+21%) and $12.89 of non-GAAP EPS (+37%), with year-end cash and short-term investments of $9.3B against $6.5B of debt.
guidanceProse: Q1 FY2027 guide (a 14-week quarter): revenue $11.1B plus or minus $0.5B (+58% YoY at the midpoint) and non-GAAP EPS $4.35 plus or minus $0.20 (+83%). On the call: Semiconductor Systems ~$8.7B, AGS ~$2.0B, Other ~$0.4B, non-GAAP gross margin ~50.8%, opex ~$1.7B, tax rate ~13%; AGS in Q2 is modelled near Q1 with opex ~15% of revenue. For calendar 2027 management gave its first outlook: wafer-fab equipment up more than 30%, Applied outgrowing the market, output rising every quarter, cloud capex up more than 50% to well over $1T, and China below 25% of the business. Supply pinch points and customer clean-room space, not orders, are the constraint; $10.8B of buyback authorization remains and the policy is to return 80-100% of free cash flow over time. No backlog figure was given and export controls were not discussed.
segments: Semiconductor Systems: $8.00B, 77% of Q4 FY2026 revenue; FY2026 $26.14B (+22%), mix foundry-logic 63%, DRAM 30%, flash 7%.
Applied Global Services: $1.90B, 18% of Q4 revenue; FY2026 $6.90B (+20%) at a 29.5% operating margin.
Other (includes Display): $517M in Q4, FY2026 $1.40B; management says to model ~$400M a quarter.
competitive: Lam Research: closest rival in deposition/etch, heavier memory/NAND mix; record $8.22B September-2026 quarter.
ASML: litho monopoly captures a growing equipment share; complementary rather than head-on.
KLA: process-control leader; Tokyo Electron competes across deposition/etch/clean.
AMAT is the largest process-equipment maker by revenue with the broadest portfolio; it targets 2+ points of share gain by 2030.

Advanced packaging: Besi/ASMPT compete in bonding; AMAT agreed in late Oct 2026 to lift its Besi stake to ~20% from 9% (subject to US antitrust review), says it serves ~80% of hybrid-bonding steps, and bought ASMPT NEXX ($120M, May 2026).
moat: Breadth is the moat: AMAT touches more materials-engineering steps than any rival, and integrated platforms plus co-optimized process flows raise switching costs at GAA/backside-power/HBM inflections. A massive installed base feeds AGS recurring revenue at ~30% operating margins, and the EPIC Center (opened Oct 2026, 15 partners including TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix, Micron and Intel) embeds AMAT in customers' next-node R&D.
catalysts: Late Jan 2027: MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META Q4 calls - 2027 capex guidance (debate 1).
Mid-Feb 2027: Q1 FY2027 report - $11.1B guide, gross margin ~50.8%, and whether Q2 is guided up on one fewer week (debates 1, 2).
Nov-Dec 2026 lame-duck session and early 2027: MATCH Act and BIS affiliates-rule action (debate 3).
Dec 2026: SEMI year-end equipment forecast vs management's 30%+ call for 2027 (debate 1).
Besi stake increase: US antitrust clearance and closing (timing unverified).

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: FY2026 free cash flow ($6.2B) is held down by capex at 7.8% of revenue and an inventory build, so a trailing FCF-DCF reads more expensive than the business is. The reverse DCF needs ~8% a year; base assumes 12% fading.
